newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela June car sales up 258 pct vs June 1996.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela June car sales up 258 pct vs June 1996.

text.p: Vehicle sales in Venezuela jumped 258.44 percent in June to 13,058 units compared to 3,643 in June 1996, the Venezuelan Automobile Chamber (CAVENEZ) said Friday.
Vehicle sales over the first half of the year were up 166 percent at 60,531 units compared to 22,756 in the first six months of 1996, the CAVENEZ figures showed.
Vehicle sales in June were also up 6.53 percent from 12,258 units in May 1997.
Following a sluggish year in 1996 as Venezuela's economy contracted 1.6 percent, vehicle sales have risen sharply to record eight consecutive months of year-on-year rises.
Government officials have pointed to the sharp hike in vehicle sales as an indication that the economy will grow by more than five percent this year.
Of the 13,058 units sold domestically in June, 11,323, or 87 percent, were assembled in Venezuela and 1,735, or 13 percent, were imported).
Of the 60,531 units sold during the first half of 1997, 51,879, or 86 percent, were assembled in Venezuela and 8,652, or 14 percent, were imported.

Vehicle exports in June rose 60.64 percent to 2,061 units from 1,283 in June 1996. Exports over the first half of 1997 were up 52.05 percent at 10,107 units, from 6,647 in the first six months of 1996.

General Motors Corp led the Venezuelan market with 31 percent of total sales in June. Ford Motor Company followed with 20 percent, Toyota Motor Corp with 14 percent, Chrysler Corp with 13 percent, Fiat SpA with nine percent and Mitsubishi Motors with nine percent and.
